result:
The proposed answer of 11 is incorrect. The solution assumes m > n, because the polynomial is written in descending order. The problem does not impose that. It only requires m ≠ n, both less than 2p, and n odd, so m < n must also be considered.

For p = 2, n can be 1 or 3, and m can be any value in {1, 2, 3} other than n. This gives these cases:
- (2,2,1) and (2,3,1) are the two cases the solution found.
- (2,1,3) gives x⁴ − 4x³ − 4x − 1, which is the same polynomial as (2,3,1), so it is reducible.
- (2,2,3) gives x⁴ − 4x³ − 4x² − 1. At x = −1 this equals 1 + 4 − 4 − 1 = 0, so it has a linear factor and is reducible.

The solution misses (2,1,3) and (2,2,3), so its total cannot be correct. The same oversight probably affects p = 3 and larger primes, since only m > n was checked there. In addition, the argument for odd primes is only asserted, not proved. A single missed case at p = 2 is enough to reject the answer.

VERDICT: REJECT
